why: The fixed input of every bench run: which cases, how many repeats, which pages. The bench has no randomness; the order is the file order. run.py records the sha256 of this file and of every case file it read in env.json.
whole_runs_why: A run is a result only when its suites are exactly one of these sets, at the reps of that set (`reps` for the first, the suite's own for the others). The three suites on the own site share a brain and are one run; each corpus suite reads public data with a brain of its own and is a run of its own.

startup.why: Brain start to /health, then the first goto (the browser starts cold). Each rep starts and stops its own scratch brain.

tools.why: The field cases of every tool (tests/field/cases/<tool>.jsonl) against the own site, through the MCP, `reps` times.

skip_ids.ws-words-edge: reaches the real search engine: a third-party answer is not reproducible, and a burst of searches got the server's address throttled before (tests/bench/INVENTORY.md)

payload.why: What one look at a page costs an agent, in tokens, against the page's own HTML fetched plainly (the baseline). A look counts only when its answer, without its own url and title, carries the words in `must` (taken from tests/field/site/server.py): a broken tool that returns 5 tokens is not a saving. `covers` says what a look returns: the whole `page` (every part of a long answer is fetched and summed; only these get a token ratio), an `outline`, the `controls` of the page, or a navigation `receipt`. The /v/ pages are the big-page fixtures (tests/field/site/fixtures.py), added 2026-10-16 so the view/read budget has a measured before.

forms.why: What the product says each field of Chromium's saved real-site forms is, against the field type Chrome's own autofill heuristics give it. Public data pinned by commit (corpora.json, corpora.lock.json); the only hand-made file is forms_vocabulary.json (which slot names mean the same as each Chrome type), reviewed before the first run. Three copies of every page are read: as saved, with a marker in every control (to learn which field is which control), and without the attributes in which the page says what a field is.
forms.reps_why: the answer is a pure function of the page and the code: a repeat would read the same fields; the suite measures what the product says, not how fast

pages.why: How well the product reads saved real article pages, scored by the public scorer of Scrapinghub's article-extraction-benchmark (evaluate.py, fetched with the data at a pinned commit and checked against the lock). The product's looks (`read(url)`; `goto` then `read(level=full)`, every part; the cheap looks `read` outline and `view` for their cost) are scored against the true article body of each page; the stubs (the page's text without markup, the title alone) are scored by the same function; five published outputs of other extractors are scored again and must come out as the repository's README table says.
pages.reps_why: The content scores (F1, precision, recall) and the token counts are a pure function of the page and the code: a repeat gives the same words (the summary says on how many pages `read(url)` gave the same words on its 3 repeats). The browser looks (goto, read outline, read full, view) each cost a near-constant 1.6 to 1.7 s of page settle on a page that runs script, so they are taken once per page; p50/p95 are over the 181 pages. `read(url)` is a plain fetch (about 50 ms) and is taken 3 times.
pages.url_reps_why: read(url) is cheap, so it is repeated: it shows whether the same words come back each time.

replay.why: What walking a saved path costs and what the product's stored route is worth through its tools, on routes fixed in replay_routes.json (the own loopback site and two public sandbox sites built for scraping). Each hop is timed and its arrival is checked by an independent read of the page; at 1, 5, 20 (and 100 on the own site) walks the stored route is asked for and the address of the last page is loaded. See suite_replay.py for what is and is not measured.
replay.reps_why: the walk repeats itself (k walks of each route are the measurement: the first against the later ones); nothing is repeated beside that

delegate.why: Whether one delegate_task call reaches a simple multi-step goal on a public practice site, and says ok only when it did: 11 goals fixed in delegate_goals.json before any change to delegate_task, each in a fresh session, each verified by an independent read of the page. See suite_delegate.py for what is and is not measured.
delegate.reps_why: delegate_goals.json holds the suite's own repeats (each goal 3 times); nothing is repeated beside that
